messages:
maya: FYI my docs PR for prompt-templates.md is blocked by a runtime question. I documented that template placeholders are auto-escaped by default (so user text can't break JSON outputs). Runtime says hosted behavior is escape-by-default but Dedicated/Private might be a config toggle. Need explicit wording and example request flag. @sam @frank

sam: Short answer: hosted default = escape_on; dedicated/private defaults depend on ops profile. There's an env VAR TEMPLATE_SAFE_MODE that controls global default. Some older dedicated installs still have it off.

frank: For clarity in docs: show the current hosted default, plus a request-level override param `template_safe_mode=false` to disable escaping for specific calls. Also show example where disabling can lead to malformed JSON in outputs.

maya: If we publish the docs saying "auto-escaped by default" without mentioning Dedicated differences, customers will be confused. Can we get the exact header or response metadata when escaping is applied?

sam: When escaping happens we include response meta `x-template-escaped: true` and we also include a small note in the response metadata `template_warnings`. Example: 

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json
x-template-escaped: true

{ "output": "...", "_meta": { "template_warnings": ["user input contained json-like fragments, auto-escaped"] } }

frank: And when strict mode is off and the template produces invalid JSON, behavior differs: hosted will still return 200 with the raw output and `x-template-escaped: false`, but Dedicated with ops-set-strict=true can return 400. So docs need to show both outcomes.

maya: Good. Also need SDK snippets for JS + python. For JS we should show how SDK exposes meta: `response.meta.template_warnings`.

sam: Agreed. One more ask: do we have a migration note for customers upgrading older Dedicated installs?

frank: Ops has a rollout note (internal) but no public doc. I'd add a migration section: "If you manage Dedicated, check TEMPLATE_SAFE_MODE env on your deployment. Upgrading may change template escaping behavior." Link to release notes when available.

maya: OK I will: 1) State hosted default = escaping on, show header `x-template-escaped`, 2) Add request-level override example "\"template_safe_mode\": false", 3) Add Dedicated/Private callout and migration note, 4) Add JS/Python SDK snippets showing meta handling.
